villain_matrix.matrix_name: Journey to the West Villain Evaluation Matrix
villain_matrix.design_purpose: Plots every monster in the book precisely onto a motivation × resources matrix, revealing the underlying law that affiliation decides fate: monsters with backing all return to their posts, while rootless nobodies are all killed or flee.

quadrants.name: Top-left
quadrants.label: Strong backing + metaphysical
quadrants.description: Top-tier backing + metaphysical motive — a rare top-tier villain, the only one in the book.
quadrants.typical_outcome: Taken in personally by senior Buddhist figures

quadrants.name: Top-right
quadrants.label: Strong backing + survival
quadrants.description: Heavenly/Buddhist establishment + mission-driven — a mountain-warlord type shielded by affiliation.
quadrants.typical_outcome: Reclaimed by their patron and restored to their post

quadrants.name: Bottom-left
quadrants.label: Weak backing + survival
quadrants.description: Rootless lone operator + instinctive survival — the classic cannon fodder, 40% of the book.

quadrants.name: Bottom-right
quadrants.label: Weak backing + metaphysical
quadrants.description: Rootless origin + metaphysical motive — an inner-demon villain, the only one in the book.

matrix_insights: Bottom-left holds 40% · all killed or driven to flee — the fate of rootless cannon fodder
Top-right holds 47% · all reclaimed by their patrons — the affiliation-as-amulet effect

Affiliation decides fate — this is the underlying law of the book's villain evaluation

rescue_roi.analysis_name: Return on Investment of Calling for Reinforcements
rescue_roi.formula: ROI = (Problem-solving efficiency × Favor spent × Marginal cost of the next request) / (Time spent × Reputation loss)

components.name: Problem-solving efficiency
components.description: How efficiently the reinforcements dispatch the demon · 10=instant kill · 1=long back-and-forth

components.name: Favor spent
components.description: The scale of favors drawn on · 10=a top bodhisattva or celestial in person · 1=minor deities

components.name: Marginal cost of next request
components.description: Prospects for long-term cooperation · 10=sustainable requests · 1=one-off expenditure

components.name: Time spent
components.description: The time cost from deciding to ask for help to resolving the problem · 10=extremely long · 1=instant

components.name: Reputation loss
components.description: How much asking for help damages one's prestige · 10=severe loss · 1=none

phase_analysis.characteristic: Fight first, ask only when losing
phase_analysis.insight: Instinctive requests · draws on top-tier resources but with weak cost awareness

phase_analysis.characteristic: Begins precise matching · but still has costly cases
phase_analysis.insight: Learning requests · starts calculating ROI but is not yet adept
Actuary-style requests · stable ROI · mature resource management

roi_insights: The Yellow Wind Demon case proves: the right remedy beats resource rank · even a minor bodhisattva can instantly dispatch a great demon
The Bull Demon King case proves: old friends turned foes + a heavenly siege = the highest cost · the emotional cost is the dearest
A late-stage ROI rebound: Wukong rises from 1.8 (Bull Demon King) to 5.0 (Lion-Camel Ridge) as he learns to calculate
Guanyin becomes the standing rescuer: diminishing marginal cost · first 2.4 → second 4.17 → third outright recruitment
The Lion-Camel Ridge case: a top-tier crisis + top-tier reinforcements = peak efficiency · the Tathagata arrives in person and instantly takes all three demons

application_scenarios.description: Harry's Dumbledore help-seeking pattern: every problem requires the headmaster himself, but after his death Harry must face Voldemort alone. ROI starts at its peak and ends at zero.
Frodo's Gandalf help-seeking pattern: Gandalf intervenes only at critical moments, and Frodo must complete the main task on his own. The most balanced ROI.
Managing upward resources: precisely match problems to a superior's domain of competence, avoid deploying top-tier resources on small problems, and build a sustainable help-seeking relationship.
Seeking investor support: early investors retain value in later rounds, and long-term partnership beats a one-off ask · diminishing marginal cost.

domino_causality.design_principle: Not arranged in chronological order · linked by butterfly effect · each fallen domino triggers the next · forming a complete causal chain
domino_causality.core_insight: The whole pilgrimage project is a precisely designed 'causal machine'

domino_chains.chain_name: The Kasaya Incident Chain · The Birth of the Golden Fillet Spell

dominos.title: Elder Jinchi Covets the Kasaya
dominos.direct_cause: Elder Jinchi covets the kasaya and sets fire to the monastery
dominos.domino_effect: Guanyin subdues the Black Bear Spirit and obtains field-test data for the Golden Fillet Spell

dominos.title: Guanyin Subdues the Black Bear Spirit
dominos.direct_cause: Wukong seeks Guanyin's help; Guanyin subdues the Black Bear Spirit with the Golden Fillet Spell
dominos.domino_effect: Provides the basis for the Tight-Fillet Spell's later effectiveness, proving the Golden Fillet Spell can control demons

dominos.title: The Tight-Fillet Spell Controls Wukong
dominos.direct_cause: Tang Sanzang uses the Tight-Fillet Spell to control and dismiss Wukong
dominos.domino_effect: After Wukong is dismissed, Tang Sanzang meets the Yellow-Robed Monster and falls into danger

dominos.title: The Yellow-Robed Monster Incident
dominos.hardship: The Letter to Precious Elephant Kingdom · The Tiger in the Golden Throne Hall
dominos.direct_cause: Tang Sanzang is captured by the Yellow-Robed Monster; Zhu Bajie goes to Flower-Fruit Mountain to bring Wukong back
dominos.domino_effect: Wukong returns; the team establishes a new power balance; the Tight-Fillet Spell becomes Wukong's 'contract'

domino_chains.chain_insight: A single moment of greed by Elder Jinchi ultimately shaped the pilgrimage team's core management tool

domino_chains.chain_name: The Wuzhuang Temple Incident Chain · The Daoist-Buddhist Alliance

dominos.title: Wukong Topples the Ginseng Fruit Tree
dominos.hardship: In Wuzhuang Temple · The Ginseng That Is Hard to Revive
dominos.direct_cause: Goaded by Bajie, Wukong topples the Ginseng Fruit Tree
dominos.domino_effect: Zhenyuanzi detains Tang Sanzang; Wukong seeks Guanyin to heal the tree

dominos.title: Guanyin Revives the Ginseng Fruit Tree
dominos.direct_cause: Guanyin revives the Ginseng Fruit Tree with sweet-dew water
dominos.domino_effect: Zhenyuanzi and Wukong become sworn brothers; the Daoists and Buddhists form a formal alliance

dominos.title: Zhenyuanzi Forms an Alliance
dominos.direct_cause: Zhenyuanzi and Wukong become sworn brothers
dominos.domino_effect: Lays the foundation for later Daoist support of the pilgrimage project; the Daoists assist in the Crow-cock Kingdom incident

domino_chains.chain_insight: A childish prank ultimately forged a strategic alliance between Daoism and Buddhism

domino_chains.chain_name: The Red Boy Incident Chain · Guanyin's Expanding Influence

dominos.title: Red Boy Seizes Tang Sanzang
dominos.hardship: The Monster at Mount Hao · The Mind-Monkey Harmed
dominos.direct_cause: Hearing that Tang Sanzang's flesh grants immortality, Red Boy captures him
dominos.domino_effect: Wukong seeks Guanyin; Guanyin takes Red Boy as the Boy of Good Wealth

dominos.title: Guanyin Subdues Red Boy
dominos.direct_cause: Guanyin subdues Red Boy with the lotus platform and the Golden Fillet Spell
dominos.domino_effect: Guanyin's influence extends to Fiery Cloud Cave, and then to 600 li of Mount Hao

dominos.title: Guanyin's Lotus Pond Expands
dominos.direct_cause: Red Boy is taken as the Boy of Good Wealth; Mount Hao is brought into Guanyin's sphere of influence
dominos.domino_effect: Foreshadows the later Goldfish Spirit incident at Tongtian River (the Goldfish Spirit escaped from Guanyin's lotus pond)

domino_chains.chain_insight: A single demon attack ultimately gave Guanyin the opportunity to expand her influence

domino_chains.chain_name: The Six-Eared Macaque Incident Chain · Discerning True from False

dominos.title: Wukong Is Dismissed Again
dominos.direct_cause: Wukong kills the bandits; Tang Sanzang dismisses Wukong again
dominos.domino_effect: Wukong harbors resentment; the Six-Eared Macaque seizes the opening

dominos.title: The Six-Eared Macaque Appears
dominos.direct_cause: The Six-Eared Macaque impersonates Wukong, wounds Tang Sanzang, and steals the luggage
dominos.domino_effect: The true-and-false Monkey King incident; even Diting cannot tell them apart, and the Buddha finally exposes the impostor

dominos.title: The Buddha Exposes the Six-Eared Macaque
dominos.direct_cause: The Buddha exposes the Six-Eared Macaque, and Wukong kills him with a single blow
dominos.domino_effect: Wukong's inner demon is eliminated; he is never dismissed again, and team relations stabilize

domino_chains.chain_insight: The Six-Eared Macaque is Wukong's inner demon; after his death, the pilgrimage team enters a new phase of the 'mind-monkey returning to order'

domino_chains.chain_name: The Lion-Camel Ridge Incident Chain · The Buddhist-Daoist Contest

dominos.title: The Green Lion Spirit Swallows Wukong
dominos.direct_cause: The Green Lion Spirit swallows Wukong, who wreaks havoc inside his belly
dominos.domino_effect: The three demons attack the pilgrimage team with full force; Wukong seeks the Buddha's help

dominos.title: The Buddha Comes in Person to Subdue the Demons
dominos.direct_cause: The Great Peng Golden-Winged Eagle is the Buddha's uncle, so the Buddha comes in person to subdue it
dominos.domino_effect: Manjushri and Samantabhadra take back the Green Lion and White Elephant; the Buddha captures the Great Peng; the Buddhist faction wins a great victory

dominos.title: The Buddhist Faction Expands
dominos.direct_cause: The three demons of Lion-Camel Ridge are subdued; the Buddhist faction takes over Lion-Camel Ridge
dominos.domino_effect: Foreshadows later Buddhist events such as the Kingdom of Dharma-Destruction and the Bhikshu Kingdom

domino_chains.chain_insight: The Battle of Lion-Camel Ridge let the Buddhist faction thoroughly suppress the Daoists, laying the foundation for Lingshan to take over the Western Cattle-Gift Continent
